extracted.intended_audience: public company registrants (issuers), their auditors and legal advisers, investors, and other stakeholders affected by SEC climate-related disclosure requirements
extracted.subtask_description: Final rules issued by the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission requiring specified climate-related disclosures in registration statements and Exchange Act annual reports (Regulation S-K subpart 1500 and Regulation S-X Article 14), including GHG metrics, governance, risk management, strategy, and certain financial statement effects, with phased compliance and assurance requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure of any material climate-related risks
rubrics_metrics.description: Any climate-related risks identified by the registrant that have had or are reasonably likely to have a material impact on the registrant, including on its strategy, results of operations, or financial condition in the short-term (i.e., the next 12 months) and in the long-term (i.e., beyond the next 12 months).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report risks that have materially affected or are reasonably likely to materially affect the business, results of operations, or financial condition; materiality is defined with respect to investors' investment and voting decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Actual and potential material impacts on strategy, business model, and outlook
rubrics_metrics.description: The actual and potential material impacts of any identified climate-related risks on the registrant's strategy, business model, and outlook, including, as applicable, any material impacts on a non-exclusive list of items.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclose how climate-related risks have or could alter the company's strategy, business model, outlook, and specific financial/operational items (use concrete examples where possible).

rubrics_metrics.name: Quantitative and qualitative disclosure of material expenditures and financial impacts from mitigation/adaptation activities
rubrics_metrics.description: If, as part of its strategy, a registrant has undertaken activities to mitigate or adapt to a material climate-related risk, a quantitative and qualitative description of material expenditures incurred and material impacts on financial estimates and assumptions that, in management's assessment, directly result from such mitigation or adaptation activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include both dollar measures and narrative explanation of how mitigation/adaptation expenditures changed financial estimates or assumptions; management must assess direct causal links.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transition plan disclosure and annual updates
rubrics_metrics.description: If a registrant has adopted a transition plan to manage a material transition risk, a description of the transition plan, and updated disclosures in the subsequent years describing the actions taken during the year under the plan, including how the actions have impacted the registrant's business, results of operations, or financial condition, and quantitative and qualitative disclosure of material expenditures incurred and material impacts on financial estimates and assumptions as a direct result of the disclosed actions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe the plan, track year-over-year actions and impacts, and disclose material expenditures and effects on financial estimates attributable to the plan; an extended safe harbor applies for certain forward-looking aspects (see safe harbor entry).

rubrics_metrics.name: Scenario analysis disclosures (when used and material)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a registrant uses scenario analysis and, in doing so, determines that a climate-related risk is reasonably likely to have a material impact on its business, results of operations, or financial condition, certain disclosures regarding such use of scenario analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclose use of scenario analysis only when it leads to the determination that a material impact is reasonably likely; provide details about scenarios, assumptions, and how outcomes inform management's assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Internal carbon price disclosures (when material)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a registrant's use of an internal carbon price is material to how it evaluates and manages a material climate-related risk, certain disclosures about the internal carbon price.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain the existence, level, application, and materiality of any internal carbon pricing and how it influences decision-making and risk management.

rubrics_metrics.name: Board oversight and management roles for climate-related risks
rubrics_metrics.description: Any oversight by the board of directors of climate-related risks and any role by management in assessing and managing the registrant's material climate-related risks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe governance structures, board oversight practices, management responsibilities, and processes used to monitor climate-related risk (the final rules adopted a less prescriptive approach here and eliminated the proposed requirement to describe board members' climate expertise).

rubrics_metrics.name: Processes for identifying, assessing, and managing material climate-related risks and integration into overall risk management
rubrics_metrics.description: Any processes the registrant has for identifying, assessing, and managing material climate-related risks and, if the registrant is managing those risks, whether and how any such processes are integrated into the registrant's overall risk management system or processes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain procedures, tools, governance linkages, and integration with enterprise risk management; be specific about how climate risks are escalated and addressed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure of climate-related targets or goals and related material expenditures/impacts
rubrics_metrics.description: If a registrant has set a climate-related target or goal that has materially affected or is reasonably likely to materially affect the registrant's business, results of operations, or financial condition, certain disclosures about such target or goal, including material expenditures and material impacts on financial estimates and assumptions as a direct result of the target or goal or actions taken to make progress toward meeting such target or goal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclose targets/goals, explain how they materially affect operations/financials, and quantify expenditures/impacts where material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope 1 and Scope 2 emissions disclosure requirement (LAFs and AFs, materiality condition)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a registrant is a large accelerated filer (LAF), or an accelerated filer (AF) that is not otherwise exempted, and its Scope 1 emissions and/or its Scope 2 emissions metrics are material, certain disclosure about those emissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scope 1/2 disclosure is required only for LAFs and AFs (not all registrants), only when emissions are material, on a phased-in basis, with exemptions for smaller reporting companies (SRCs) and emerging growth companies (EGCs); registrants may have the option to provide disclosure on a delayed basis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attestation requirement for disclosed Scope 1 and Scope 2 emissions (phased assurance levels)
rubrics_metrics.description: A registrant that is required to disclose Scopes 1 and/or 2 emissions and is an LAF or AF must file an attestation report in respect of those emissions subject to phased in compliance dates. An AF must file an attestation report at the limited assurance level beginning the third fiscal year after the compliance date for disclosure of GHG emissions. An LAF must file an attestation report at the limited assurance level beginning the third fiscal year after the compliance date for disclosure of GHG emissions, and then file an attestation report at the reasonable assurance level beginning the seventh fiscal year after the compliance date for disclosure of GHG emissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attestation reports must be filed with the GHG emissions disclosures in the same filing; voluntary disclosures of emissions that are subjected to third-party assurance must include certain related disclosures (see voluntary assurance entry).

rubrics_metrics.name: Financial statement disclosures focused on capitalized costs, expenditures expensed, charges, and losses from severe weather events
rubrics_metrics.description: The capitalized costs, expenditures expensed, charges, and losses incurred as a result of severe weather events and other natural conditions, such as hurricanes, tornadoes, flooding, drought, wildfires, extreme temperatures, and sea level rise, subject to applicable one percent and de minimis disclosure thresholds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such disclosures are required in a note to the registrant's audited financial statements and the final rules focus required disclosure of financial statement effects on these categories rather than requiring disclosure of impacts on each line item of the consolidated financial statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure of capitalized costs, expenditures, and losses related to carbon offsets and RECs when material
rubrics_metrics.description: The capitalized costs, expenditures expensed, and losses related to carbon offsets and renewable energy credits or certificates ("RECs") if used as a material component of a registrant's plans to achieve its disclosed climate-related targets or goals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report amounts and explain how offsets/RECs materially factor into plans for meeting targets/goals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Qualitative description of impacts on development of financial statement estimates and assumptions
rubrics_metrics.description: If the estimates and assumptions a registrant uses to produce the financial statements were materially impacted by risks and uncertainties associated with severe weather events and other natural conditions, such as hurricanes, tornadoes, flooding, drought, wildfires, extreme temperatures, and sea level rise, or any disclosed climate-related targets or transition plans, a qualitative description of how the development of such estimates and assumptions was impacted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe how severe weather or climate targets influenced selection or calibration of accounting estimates/assumptions (e.g., valuation, impairment, reserve estimates).

rubrics_metrics.name: Presentation, submission, and electronic tagging requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: File the climate-related disclosure in its registration statements and Exchange Act annual reports; include the climate-related disclosures required under Regulation S-K in a separate, appropriately captioned section of its filing or in another appropriate section (e.g., Risk Factors, Description of Business, or MD&A), or by incorporation by reference from another Commission filing as long as the disclosure meets the electronic tagging requirements of the final rules; electronically tag both narrative and quantitative climate-related disclosures in Inline XBRL.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permits flexibility of placement (separate "Climate-Related Disclosure" section or incorporation by reference) but requires Inline XBRL tagging for both narrative and numeric disclosures; tagging requirement applies to disclosures regardless of location if incorporated by reference and tagged.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing and location rules for Scope 1 and Scope 2 emissions disclosures
rubrics_metrics.description: If required to disclose its Scopes 1 and 2 emissions, provide such disclosure for the registrant's most recently completed fiscal year and, to the extent previously disclosed, for the historical fiscal year(s) included in the filing; specific timing/location: domestic filers in Form 10-K (or via Form 10-Q for second fiscal quarter incorporated by reference), foreign private issuers on Form 20-F due no later than 225 days after fiscal year end, and registration statements must include emissions for the most recently completed fiscal year at least 225 days prior to effectiveness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the specified form/timing rules depending on domestic vs. foreign filer status; historical years required if previously disclosed or otherwise applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Safe harbor for certain forward-looking climate-related disclosures
rubrics_metrics.description: The final rules provide a safe harbor for climate-related disclosures pertaining to transition plans, scenario analysis, the use of an internal carbon price, and targets and goals ... all information required by the specified sections, except for historical facts, is considered a forward-looking statement for purposes of the PSLRA safe harbors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Forward-looking aspects of transition plans, scenario analysis, internal carbon pricing, and targets/goals (other than historical facts) receive PSLRA protection; companies should still ensure reasonable bases for such statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Materiality-qualified and less-prescriptive approach to certain disclosures
rubrics_metrics.description: The final rules adopt a less prescriptive approach to certain disclosures (e.g., climate-related risk disclosure, board oversight disclosure, and risk management disclosure requirements) and qualify requirements to provide certain climate-related disclosures based on materiality (e.g., disclosures regarding impacts of climate-related risks, use of scenario analysis, and maintained internal carbon price).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclosure obligations are bounded by materiality; the Commission eliminated overly prescriptive proposals such as mandatory description of board members' climate expertise and the universal requirement to disclose Scopes 1 and 2 for all registrants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exemptions, scaled requirements, and phased compliance by filer category
rubrics_metrics.description: The final rules are phased in with the compliance date dependent upon the status of the registrant as an LAF, an AF, a non-accelerated filer (NAF), SRC, or EGC, and the content of the disclosure; SRCs and EGCs are exempted from the Scope 1 and Scope 2 emissions disclosure requirement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify filer category to determine compliance dates, phased assurance requirements, and whether exemptions or scaled requirements apply; phase-in periods were extended in response to comments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of voluntary GHG emissions disclosures
rubrics_metrics.description: A registrant that is not required to disclose its GHG emissions or to include a GHG emissions attestation report pursuant to the final rules must disclose certain information if the registrant voluntarily discloses its GHG emissions in a Commission filing and voluntarily subjects those disclosures to third-party assurance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Voluntary emission disclosures that are subjected to third-party assurance trigger additional disclosure obligations (e.g., disclosure of the assurance and related information); companies should coordinate voluntary reporting with attestations and filing requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Placement of financial statement climate-related disclosures in audited financial statement notes
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide the financial statement disclosures required under Regulation S-X for the registrant's most recently completed fiscal year, and to the extent previously disclosed or required to be disclosed, for the historical fiscal year(s) included in the filing, in a note to the registrant's audited financial statements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Financial impact metrics, expenditure metrics, and financial estimates/assumptions affected by climate-related matters should appear as notes in audited financial statements per Regulation S-X (Article 14) rather than scattered across filings.
